answer_1.quote: Automatic release note generation can be viewed as a task of summarizing commit messages ... we introduce Classwise Extractive‑then‑Abstractive Summarization (CEAS) and Classwise Abstractive Summarization (CAS) models ...

answer_2.quote: Following the conventional summarization literature, we employ ROUGE as the automatic evaluation metric. We also employ BLEU to evaluate the fluency of generated release notes. Specifically, we compute ROUGE‑L (F1), BLEU‑3, and BLEU‑4 scores. ... We also compute Specificity, i.e., TN/(TN+FP).

answer_4.quote: We employed twelve human evaluators to manually assess the quality of the release notes generated by the systems and the reference release notes ... We used a five‑point scoring scheme for evaluating the release notes. The evaluation scores were determined based on two criteria: Percentage of necessary information (coverage) and percentage of unnecessary information (noise contamination).
answer_4.guideline: Five‑point scoring scheme covering coverage (percentage of necessary information) and noise (percentage of unnecessary information).
